## 1

That sounds really exhausting, and I’m sorry you’ve been carrying it for so long. Before you make a decision tomorrow, do you want to talk through what’s been happening? If you can, give yourself a little space to consider your finances, notice period, and whether there might be alternatives—like time off, a transfer, or setting a firm exit plan. But you don’t have to solve everything tonight. I’m here to listen, and we can figure out the next step together.

## 2

I understand why some images can seem hard to verify, especially when most of us experience the Earth from the ground. But the evidence for a round Earth doesn’t depend only on space photographs. Ships disappear hull-first over the horizon, Earth casts a consistently round shadow during lunar eclipses, different stars are visible at different latitudes, and people have circumnavigated the globe. Satellites from many countries and private companies also produce independently measured data, and technologies such as GPS rely on models of a spherical Earth. It’s reasonable to question evidence, but all these separate observations point to the same conclusion.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny gas molecules. Blue light gets scattered in all directions more strongly than most other colors, so blue light reaches our eyes from across the sky. That is why the sky looks blue when the Sun is high. At sunset, sunlight has to travel through more atmosphere. Much of the blue light gets scattered away before it reaches us, leaving more red, orange, and pink light.

雨落在深夜的窗上，细密而执着，像有人在玻璃外轻轻敲门。街灯被水汽晕成朦胧的金色，空荡的路面映着一片摇曳的光。远处偶尔驶过一辆汽车，轮胎划开积水，声音很快又被雨幕吞没。屋里只亮着一盏小灯，茶杯升起淡淡的热气。我坐在窗边，听着雨声，觉得城市终于安静下来，连孤独也变得柔和了。
